R5 (diagnosis 11 §17): a reply marked through `actionpressure` is drawn marked, read from `pressurefor`, and not offered again; another received reply still offers it

R12: the marks are paged by `after`: the next page is read from the cursor until none follows

R17: a machine proposal is drawn only while the assistant is reachable, apart and labelled; a member's whether or not; control: it is not the tier

outside.waitsOn: interface-shell: the item in its interface files
tests: R5: reads the action: what it is, to whom (by role, with who holds it today), when and by whom it was sent, its replies; the wait while one is owed
R5 (action-producers R1; v0.2 rule 6): each due date is drawn with mark.due and opens due-date; a passed one is canon's question, never 'overdue' until a member determines it
R5: 'Record a reply' sends actioncorrespond with the day and the member's account; 'Mark a reply as pressure' marks a received one once
R5 (diagnosis 11 §17): a reply marked through `actionpressure` is drawn marked, read from `pressurefor`, and not offered again; another received reply still offers it
R5: 'Move the action' to a state its edges allow, with the reason in the query actions reads; resolving names how
R5: 'Remind me' on a dated entry; confidential or not with a reason, a published case keeping what it said; the litigation hold is no longer placed here (R32)
R10 (DEC-212): an action holding an approved, unsent text offers to pick up where it was left, opening the request at its send step; control: none without one
R12: the action heads the screen with its title and its project as a reference, each as `action` answers them; control: a null is drawn absent, never as 'untitled'
R12: the pressure marks from pressurefor are drawn with where each arrived; control: a mark on another action is not drawn
R12: the marks are paged by `after`: the next page is read from the cursor until none follows
R16: the law chosen is drawn by level and citation with its window and who stated it, and when; a proposal is drawn apart, never as the law
R16: an undetermined list is drawn as law.undetermined; control: nothing is drawn as stated
R16: 'Change the law…' sends actionlaws with the law chosen from those the group's places name; 'Propose another law…' sends actionlawspropose and changes nothing
R16: refusals are drawn by their words, beside the act
R17: tier 2 is drawn by key with its words, its latest revision (who, when, the reason, the prior tier's words); control: tier undetermined has its own words
R17: 'Revise, with a reason…' sends actionrisktier with the tier and the reason; its refusals are drawn by their words
R17: a machine proposal is drawn only while the assistant is reachable, apart and labelled; a member's whether or not; control: it is not the tier

R23, R26: where a reply's date has passed with none recorded, 'Open a question from this' is offered at once with a field for the question; it sends actioninquiry, the page stays and says where the question is open, with a reference to it
R23: on request on any action: a date not yet passed offers it behind a fold, with no 'no reply recorded' box; control: it is the same act
R23: ACTION_NO_PROJECT, MACHINE_CANNOT_OPEN_FROM_ACTION and ACTION_INQUIRY_NO_QUESTION are drawn by their words, beside the act; an action in no project opens nothing

outside.waitsOn: this module
tests: R5: reads the action: what it is, to whom (by role, with who holds it today), when and by whom it was sent, its replies; the wait while one is owed
R5 (action-producers R1; v0.2 rule 6): each due date is drawn with mark.due and opens due-date; a passed one is canon's question, never 'overdue' until a member determines it
R5: 'Record a reply' sends actioncorrespond with the day and the member's account; 'Mark a reply as pressure' marks a received one once
R5 (diagnosis 11 §17): a reply marked through `actionpressure` is drawn marked, read from `pressurefor`, and not offered again; another received reply still offers it
R5: 'Move the action' to a state its edges allow, with the reason in the query actions reads; resolving names how
R5: 'Remind me' on a dated entry; confidential or not with a reason, a published case keeping what it said; the litigation hold is no longer placed here (R32)
R10 (DEC-212): an action holding an approved, unsent text offers to pick up where it was left, opening the request at its send step; control: none without one
R12: the action heads the screen with its title and its project as a reference, each as `action` answers them; control: a null is drawn absent, never as 'untitled'
R12: the pressure marks from pressurefor are drawn with where each arrived; control: a mark on another action is not drawn
R12: the marks are paged by `after`: the next page is read from the cursor until none follows
R16: the law chosen is drawn by level and citation with its window and who stated it, and when; a proposal is drawn apart, never as the law
R16: an undetermined list is drawn as law.undetermined; control: nothing is drawn as stated
R16: 'Change the law…' sends actionlaws with the law chosen from those the group's places name; 'Propose another law…' sends actionlawspropose and changes nothing
R16: refusals are drawn by their words, beside the act
R17: tier 2 is drawn by key with its words, its latest revision (who, when, the reason, the prior tier's words); control: tier undetermined has its own words
R17: 'Revise, with a reason…' sends actionrisktier with the tier and the reason; its refusals are drawn by their words
R17: a machine proposal is drawn only while the assistant is reachable, apart and labelled; a member's whether or not; control: it is not the tier

R23, R26: where a reply's date has passed with none recorded, 'Open a question from this' is offered at once with a field for the question; it sends actioninquiry, the page stays and says where the question is open, with a reference to it
R23: on request on any action: a date not yet passed offers it behind a fold, with no 'no reply recorded' box; control: it is the same act
R23: ACTION_NO_PROJECT, MACHINE_CANNOT_OPEN_FROM_ACTION and ACTION_INQUIRY_NO_QUESTION are drawn by their words, beside the act; an action in no project opens nothing

outside.waitsOn: interface-shell: the item in its interface files
tests: R1–R6, R9 (interface-shell R21): SCREENS is the registry screens plan, start-send, request, action, matter, help-records, each {id, reads, render, acts, words}
R1–R6 (interface-shell R21, R38): each screen's acts are exactly its registry acts, every op in OPS, each with its send
R20 to R23, R19: the keys each new requirement names are the module's, each one setup-words holds, on the screen that draws it
R19 (setup-words R12, R13): the module holds keys only: SCREEN_WORDS is a list of keys, each one setup-words holds, and each screen's words are keys of it or of the acts' and the shell's
R19: over fixtures, what a screen draws for a sample of its keys equals word(key, vars): the plan's, the action's and the matter's
R7 (action-producers R19): every member-facing sentence calls a plan's subject a matter: no word a screen draws says 'subject' of a plan
R7 (interface-shell R23): no place is named in the words this module reads
R1–R6, R9 (interface-shell R8, R21): the shell serves the six screens: each route draws its screen under its path, from its own source
R7 (interface-shell R5, R10): every text node each screen draws, with data, empty and failed, is a word (filled) or the record's own data
R19: no screen draws a placeholder: every {name} of a word it reads is filled, in every state the fixtures reach
R7 (interface-shell R10): a failed read is drawn as failed, never as empty, on every screen
R7 (interface-shell R12, R15, R22): an act the gate refuses is absent, never greyed; no explanation inside another; every control named, every field labelled
R7 (interface-shell R13): each refusal word an act names is a listed word
R7: after an act the screen re-reads what it changed: an act names only its own screen's reads
R1–R6 (interface-shell R8): every working screen is drawn under its path, its project's step named by the project's title as read
R14: every element these screens draw uses a class a served stylesheet defines (civicsmith.css, the design page's product rules, the shell's own style); none of mk-form, mk-done, mk-grid, cs-form
R14: every labelled field is the kit's cs.field (or cs.choice): a label sits only in a .cs-field, and no help sits outside one
R14: a section, list or reading that holds nothing is not drawn, and no count is drawn at zero: each screen over an empty fixture
R14 (control; interface-shell R10): a read that failed is still drawn as failed, on every screen

tests: R37: a sent action with no clock entry draws a reference to `due-date` for it, with the card's name and purpose; control: with entries the dates link as before and no such reference is added
R40: `action` draws a reference opening `counsel` for the action, its card the screen's name and purpose
R43: any unsent action draws the door to `start-send`, where its text is prepared; a sent one does not
R38: the reply form sends actioncorrespond with each field under the name `actions` declares; every field the design holds a word for is drawn
R38: a reply needs its day and a received one its account; a refusal is drawn by its words and the form keeps what was typed
R52 (L21): after `reminderset` the entry shows the day the member set, by key; control: a refused day shows its refusal and no reminder

R54, R59 (E3; DEC-439 E H1b): 'Change the law…' and 'Propose another law…' share one list of laws (`law.pick`) drawn once with both acts under it; each act sends the chosen law with the fields its owner declares; control: no laws draws neither act
R37, R38, R40, R43, R52, R54 (R19): each key the new lines name is a word of setup-words, on the screen that draws it

R55 control: an action of another kind draws no fold and sends no `minutes`
R55 control: no part of the minutes sends none; a part missing is refused in place and sends nothing; words the document does not hold are refused; a silence carries none
R55: a recorded entry's minutes are said beside it with `screen.action.minutes.says`, its meeting and its day

R39, R46 (R19): each key the new lines name is a word of setup-words, on the screen that draws it

outside.waitsOn: action-holds: the item in its interface files
tests: R32: `hold` reads `holdsdue` for where the pressure arrived (a reply, a docket entry, pressure outside any action) and the counsel matters from `projectlist`, each marked with no hold placed
R32: the docket marks and counsel matters are places the hold may be placed at
R32: placing the hold sends the place chosen and the reason, any projects it may also reach, and asks no approval; the hold notice is prepared on its own screen
R32: releasing a hold is drawn on `hold`: the place, the member's reason in `screen.hold.release.reason`, confirmed because it cannot be undone

R32 (A1): a reply's hold, placed by the real `actionhold`, is no longer a place to place one (`holdsdue` drops it) and is a place to release, with what the release restarts read first; releasing sends the place and the reason and the store holds it released
R32 (B46, action-holds R22): a hold placed from a docket mark is listed in place from `holdsplaced`, previewed and released with the body that placed it (`from` included), and then listed released
R32: pressure that arrived outside any action is recorded in a project, creating no action; `actionhold` is no longer drawn on `action`
R33: 'Prepare the notice' fills the field with the notice as prepared, editable, and sends no other act; a released hold prepares none
R33: 'Record that I sent it' sends the day, how it was sent and the copy or account inside the outward dialog, and no recipient, read or compliance; the screen says so
R34: the counsel packet: its two names, the purpose, the reason; counsel required at tier 3 or undetermined, optional at 1 or 2; the packet is never offered for publication

R34: each matter as the packet states it, 'not determined' never stopping the packet; a claim draws no defense sections, a defense adds the challenged statements, pressure and deadlines; every section is marked
R32 (diagnosis 11 §16): each place in 'The hold is for' is named by its mark's note and day, so two marks of one day read apart

tests: R36: what is available by tier draws one row per kind of the answer {kinds, determinations, says}, never one blank row
R45 (b): a matter with no determination yet draws each act that needs one as unavailable, saying why, and offers to record a determination

R45 (c): recording a determination sends exactly what `determine` declares: the act, the findings it rests on, the rule, what it requires and what was done, the outcome, the question when unclear, the cause
R45 (C6): the event, the passage and the finding are chosen among what the project holds, and a determination missing one is refused in the words that name it
R45 (d): revising a determination names the one it replaces, opens with its values, and says why in the reason; the earlier is not edited

R45: a determination already replaced is read and offers no form to record, revise or add to
R50: what the breach did is recorded with the rule it breached, who was affected, what it is measured in, the period and how it is known; each act sends its declared fields
R50: a recorded part is revised with the reason, only what was changed sent; control: the reason is the member's own
R50: whether a part was addressed is recorded with its evidence, its reason and, for an addressed one, in what way; control: a part not addressed names no way
R50: a success is recognised with what changed, when, the evidence, the order of events and, if said, the cause; control: the optional ones left out are not sent
R50: ending an escalation is refused in words while compliance is not restored or the consequences are undetermined or not addressed; control: an ended one draws no refusal
R51: an action is attached to the stage with the member's reason, picked from the determination's actions; at the political accountability stage with its purpose and the rules it seeks enforced

R51: pausing sends the reason; a paused escalation proposes nothing and is resumed, the reason optional; each only in its own state
R51: the government's response is read at the response evaluation stage, from the replies received on the attached actions, with a reading and a reason
R51: stages are named in words, never shown by number: the ladder and the forms of each stage draw the stage's own word

R45 (writinghelp control): a help button that names no act sends no help request
R45, R50, R51 (R19): each form draws its sentences by their keys, and every act of the screen is explained by its own word

R45 (DEC-387): revising reads 'Revise the determination' and 'What it replaces'; the rule's choice is 'Rule'

R50 (DEC-387): consequences read the matter's kinds and units, 'Describe them', 'Not known yet' and the reason behind a fold 'If you assess it yourself'; addressing reads 'The part', 'This part was' and 'Can't be undone'; a success reads 'When it changed'

R51 (DEC-387): attaching at the political accountability stage reads 'Its purpose' and its five options by key; the response reads the three readings by key and 'No response' for the reply; pausing reads 'Pause it'
R6 (DEC-387): the stages are named without a number: 'Move on to the next stage' carries the stage's name, and a stage listed on an action is 'at' its name

this module: code the checker accepts under the standard's settings
tests: R44 (c) (C53-min): choosing an option with a reminder day and the date list left blank succeeds: the reminder is for the option's first date; control: a date picked is the one sent, and no day sends no reminder
R44 (c) (C53-min): the picked options chosen together with a day and no date each take their own first date; an option with no date takes none
R20 (C64-more): an office named by its agency alone (no comma, no office within it) is drawn once; the two fields are the agency and the office within it, the entity labelled by both
R20 (C64-more): naming the same office again returns the first entry, which is the one chosen; a different office within the same agency is another entry
R4, R9 (C64-law): the law picker lists the profile's records laws, each with its own first-request window, never the deadlines; the federal law goes with its level

R9 (C64-law): the help for a federal request names 5 U.S.C. § 552(a)(6)(A)(i) and its 20 business days, no state or city statute and no 'the city'; control: a California request keeps its statute and window
R9 (C64-law): the request page's help link carries the action, so the help is for the law chosen
R9 (C64-law): the send step and the reply form say nothing of 'the city' for a federal request; control: the state's law and an undetermined law keep their wording
R9 (C64-law): the action's due dates name the kind in the profile's words, never a rule's code; an entry with no words of the profile's is not drawn as a code
R3, R8 (C64-template): a typed plain request prepares: the period, form and cost are sent only where the text names those blanks; control: a text naming all three sends all three
R3, R8 (C64-template): when the kind holds no template the request says so in words and never 'Drafted from your team's template'; control: with a template offered it says that

R16, R54, R4 (C64-law): 'Change the law…' on a records request lists the records laws and sends the chosen law's own level; a law that states no level asks for one; control: other kinds list their deadlines' laws as before

R43, R48, R59 (C65; DEC-439 E H2): a request prepared, approved, sent and answered offers the way to keep its filing as the team's template: the action draws the reference, it opens `start-send`, which draws the form; control: an unsent action and an action with no filing do not
R27, R43, R48 (C65): a member who may read and not act is shown no way to keep the filing as a template (the control is an act); control: a member who may act is

R20, R4 (C64, DEC-402): with no office known a member names one: the fold, then `entitycreate` with the office, where requests go and the law, the office drawn marked and chosen, and 'Start the request' addressed to it

R20 (C64): where requests go is sent as an email, a portal or an address by its form, and not at all when left empty; a refused office chooses none; control: a profile with no records law draws no law choice and sends none
R20 (C64): the administrator's wording is unchanged and she keeps Places; control: with offices known the fold is not drawn
R31 (C66): 'Show the routes' with none says that none is known for the kind, not only 'Nothing here'; control: a kind with routes lists them and says no such thing

R7 (interface-shell R23): no place is named in the words this module reads

R7 (interface-shell R10): a failed read is drawn as failed, never as empty, on every screen

R7 (interface-shell R13): each refusal word an act names is a listed word

tests: R44 (a): 'Add an option' sends the declared names only: with nothing more given it sends the line, kind and matter alone (no addressee, dates, tier, lobbying or enforces)
R44 (a): the addressee is sent as the plane's shape for each of the five choices, never a private individual; 'no one in particular' sends none
R44 (a): the dates that bind an option each carry their basis; 'add another' (up to 20) adds a line; an empty line sends nothing
R44 (a): the tier is sent only when one is chosen ('not assessed yet' sends none); lobbying sends the mark and the requirement it seeks
R44 (a): each refusal of 'Add an option' is drawn by its two sentences, beside the act; control: an option the plane takes draws none
R44 (b): a scenario lays out more than one phase, each with its name, options, start, check-back days, test and where each judgement goes
R44 (b): each refusal of a scenario is drawn by its two sentences, beside the act; control: a scenario the plane takes draws none
R44 (c): an option can be marked done or blocked, or returned to undecided, each sending its reason; never the mark it already has
R44 (c): a reminder (which date of the option, on what day) goes with the choice; none asked sends none; control: no dates, no reminder control
R44 (c): each refusal of a decision is drawn by its words beside the act: no reason, a reminder that is not for a choice or names no date of the option, no such option, a closed plan
R53: an option with no summary is named by its place in the list, a phase with no name by its place in its scenario, never by an id, wherever it is drawn
R53: the Judge control is drawn only once the checkpoint is due, by the page's clock; before, the day it can be judged; control: due today or earlier draws Judge
R53: a judgement is drawn as the words 'met' and 'not met', never the raw value: the judged phase, the control's choices and the check that a judgement leads nowhere
R44 (registry): the assistant's help with words is drawn on the option's line and detail and the close note only while the assistant is reachable; control: unreachable draws none

R44 (DEC-387): 'Add an option' reads the design's rows: the kinds, who it is directed to, the role and the date, the tier, seeking enforcement and its 'None'; control: the case list is not the table's

R44 (DEC-387): deciding the options reads the design's rows: marking done and blocked and returning to undecided on a row; 'Choose them', 'Decline them' and 'Mark them blocked' on the picked ones; the reminder's 'Which date'
R44 (DEC-387): a scenario's phase reads the design's rows: 'A phase', its options, when it starts, which phase and 'No phase' for where each judgement goes

R1, R44 (c) (C53): a chosen option with dates draws the Set-reminder act and the day it holds, read from the record; the act sends the choice with the reminder; control: an option with none draws the act only

R1, R7: 'Add a matter' sends plansubjectadd with the matter and the member's reason, its label the key's word; control: no reference sends nothing
R1: optionadd sends the option's line, category and matter; optionadopt adopts a suggestion or a standing offer only by the member's act
R1: scenarioset lays out a scenario of chosen options; checkpointrecord judges a checkpoint; refusals stay beside the act
R1 (v0.2 rule 18): 'Take this up' routes the item's to-dos to the member, nobody assigned; the screen then says she took it up
R1: 'Start…' opens start-send for the chosen option, sending nothing; 'Close plan…' sends planclose with the reason and the lessons
R1: control: a closed plan offers no act
R13: 'Ask the assistant for options' sends planask with the plan, labelled by its key, its run drawn running; control: no optionpropose is sent
R15: the help drawn for the ask is act.planask.does's, never act.optionpropose.does's
R13: the run is re-read on the page clock until it ends, and its proposals then reach the tray, labelled machine work; an ended run is not read again
R13: existed: true draws the run already asked; a refusal is drawn beside the act, and nothing is drawn as asked
R13: a closed plan offers no ask; the ask is drawn only while the assistant is reachable
R18 (D5, D29): an answer of ok: true that carries started: false (no run already asked), dispatched: false or withheld is drawn as its refusal, never as a run looking for options
R18: 'looking for options' is drawn only while airun answers the run as running; control: an ended run does not, and nothing is drawn before airun answers
R18 (D20): the plan names its project and its questions by their titles, each a reference; never INQ-… or inquiry:INQ-…
R18: a reference is picked from a list the record answers, never typed; what the plan holds is not offered again; control: with nothing to pick, no field and no act
R18: categories are drawn by their words, never as lowercase codes: a category the plan does not know is the word for other

tests: R4, R39: says to look first (a public record is captured instead), asks which name the records concern, then 'Choose the office' brings the offices and 'Start the request', which creates the action and opens it
R20, R39: with no office known the request says so and points an administrator to Places and offices, and draws no later step; control: a member sees no reference, a team with offices draws R4's flow
R4: the law it goes under is chosen among the laws the profile names for a records request, each with its window
R4, R8: 'Prepare the text' sends communicationprepare with the period, the form and the cost limit, those the text names, as fills; 'Approve this text' then follows
R8: the outward warning names that the portal shows the text to anyone; 'I have sent it' takes the portal's request number; control: a malformed number is refused in words
R10 (DEC-212): an action opened at its address opens at the step it has reached: approved and not sent opens at the send; control: nothing prepared opens at the text
R4: control: an action already sent draws its sending and offers no act of the flow but the law
R11: a request reloaded between preparing and approving draws the same text and fills; control: nothing is prepared again by reading
R21: request draws 'Sent with' (the team's name and its statement) and 'In this matter' with the stake and its source, above the approval, and no question
R21: the stake shown is the action's own when it has one, else the project's, else 'none beyond the team's'; control: one that cannot be read says so and is never none
R21: nothing waits on the stake on request: preparing, approving and recording the sending are drawn whether or not it can be read

R48: the template's refusals are drawn by their words beside the act; control: a save that lands draws none

R3, R41: start-send's acts are exactly its registry acts; writing help is drawn beside the own-words fields only while the assistant is reachable and sends the declared names

outside.waitsOn: this module
tests: R41, R59 (DEC-439 J43): filingprepare answered FILING_TIER_UNDETERMINED draws its refusal words and, beside them, a reference to the action's risk (risk.title) that opens the action screen on this action; control: success and other refusals draw none

R42: a refusal ASSERTION_UNRESOLVED draws one choice per pointed-out sentence, with the design's words; the resend carries `resolutions` of the declared shape (the exact text, `only_asks` with words, `breach_claim` without), never an `index`

R42: a sentence answered on one refusal stays answered on the next, so the resend carries every resolution; one left open is not sent; control: a resolution of a sentence no longer in the text is not sent
R42: a refusal ASSERTION_RESOLUTION_REFUSED is drawn by its words and keeps the choices' place; control: an approval that is not refused sends only `filing`, and `text` where she edited it

R42 (B16 a, DEC-387): a refusal CONTRADICTED_HELD draws 'A sentence the record contradicts' for each sentence, with a reason and a tick, and no act of its own; the resend carries `release: [{ord, reason}]` for the ticked ones, the shape `filings` declares
R42 (B16 a): after the approval lands the release is said once, by key, with who and when; control: an approval that is not refused sends no `release`, and draws none
R47: the start step offers the team's contact, optional, 'No one yet' first, from the members the plane lists; the choice sends `contact`, no choice sends none
R47: CONTACT_NOT_A_MEMBER is drawn by its words beside the act and the form is kept; control: a start that lands draws none
L20: optionstart refused ACTION_BASIS_REFUSED draws the code's words and then each finding's detail, as the record answers it (escaped); control: no findings draws the code's sentence only
R48: 'Keep this filing as your team's template' is offered once the filing is approved (the send step) and sends the declared names: filing, name, use and notes; not before approval
R48: offered at every step from approval: waiting for the second approval, the send, and after the sending; control: a name that is empty is refused in place and sends nothing
R48: a filing that needs counsel first (tier 3, by the draft, the action or the stake read) is offered only as a brief; control: a tier 2 filing is offered both
R48: the template's refusals are drawn by their words beside the act; control: a save that lands draws none
R49: each exhibit's grade and what the venue accepts is drawn from the prepared filing's answer: within, contestable, below, undetermined; a flagged exhibit never stops the approval
R49: where the venue's standard is not stated its fold is drawn and the grades still show; control: a stated standard draws no fold, and a filing with no exhibits draws no section

R49 (filings R59, R25): after a reload the exhibits and the venue's standard are drawn from the stored draft `filingread` answers; control: a row stored before they existed (exhibits [] and no standard) draws no section
R3, R41: start-send's acts are exactly its registry acts; writing help is drawn beside the own-words fields only while the assistant is reachable and sends the declared names

R57, R20, R59 (re-walk 10 N3; DEC-439 N3): the fold that names an office says so when the team holds no body to tie it to, and where one is added; once a body is held it is offered and the sentence is gone
R56, R53 (re-walk 10): a phase that addresses someone outside with no branch for a hostile response is drawn in the design's own sentence, with the phase by name, never the plane's
R56 (re-walk 10 N7): a refusal of what an action rests on or advances, with the owner's reasons, draws those reasons whole and not the code's sentence that tells her to leave it out
R56 (re-walk 10 N7): the same when starting an option's action is refused; control: a refusal with no reasons draws the code's sentence alone

R56 (walk E C2a (1, 2)): a noncompliant determination against a standard whose binding is undetermined is drawn in the owner's words with the owner's why, never as 'does not bind'; the body is chosen among the team's offices and bodies and sent as the entity id
R56 (walk E C2b): the project's determinations are drawn each with its standards' outcomes, and recording one goes to its page
R56 (walk C C-M11): a concluded question no published case holds is drawn as concluded and never tickable; a published finding is offered as before

R56 (walk E K-words): a date check that cannot be told for want of a day names its option and phase by name, in the design's words, never ids; a regulated date before its phase draws names and days as dates
R56, R59 (walk E K4; walk C C-M17; DEC-439 K4): an option to an office, the press or an organization with its role or its body empty draws the owner's refusal naming the empty part
R56 (walk E K-new): a request for comment with no advancing leg is sent and the plane's own refusal, with its findings, is drawn; the leg defaults to 'Advances'
R56 (walk E K10): the door to the risk beside the tier refusal is its own control after the sentence, not run on from it; control: no refusal draws none
R56 (walk E H2): after a filing is recorded sent, its proposed next state is said in the owner's words with the way to the action's move; before, none
R56 (walk E H1): a request offers the team's named offices again, picked by label and asked about, and an empty press is refused in words, never silent
R56 (walk E K12): 'Waiting on' is drawn only while the action is neither resolved nor abandoned, whatever the plane says is owed
R58: a project with no dated event draws, in place of the event picker, the sentence that says so and where to record one; control: a project with an event draws the picker and not the sentence
R58: with no finding held to rest a determination on, the determination says so above Record a determination; control: with a published finding it does not
R58 (walk C C-M11): a concluded question no published case holds says it is concluded and not yet a finding, beside its title; control: with none such, the sentence is absent
R58: the determination's body is a choice among the team's offices and bodies, helped by its sentence; control: with the body read failed, neither the choice nor the help is drawn
R36: what is available by tier draws one row per kind of the answer {kinds, determinations, says}, never one blank row
R45 (b): a matter with no determination yet draws each act that needs one as unavailable, saying why, and offers to record a determination

R45 (c): recording a determination sends exactly what `determine` declares: the act, the findings it rests on, the rule, what it requires and what was done, the outcome, the question when unclear, the cause
R45 (C6): the event, the passage and the finding are chosen among what the project holds, and a determination missing one is refused in the words that name it
R45 (d): revising a determination names the one it replaces, opens with its values, and says why in the reason; the earlier is not edited
R45: the determination's refusals are drawn by their words (refusal.<CODE>); control: a recorded one draws none
R45: a member who may not act reads the read-only sentence and is offered no form and no act
R45: a determination already replaced is read and offers no form to record, revise or add to
R50: what the breach did is recorded with the rule it breached, who was affected, what it is measured in, the period and how it is known; each act sends its declared fields
R50: a recorded part is revised with the reason, only what was changed sent; control: the reason is the member's own
R50: whether a part was addressed is recorded with its evidence, its reason and, for an addressed one, in what way; control: a part not addressed names no way
R50: a success is recognised with what changed, when, the evidence, the order of events and, if said, the cause; control: the optional ones left out are not sent
R50: ending an escalation is refused in words while compliance is not restored or the consequences are undetermined or not addressed; control: an ended one draws no refusal
R51: an action is attached to the stage with the member's reason, picked from the determination's actions; at the political accountability stage with its purpose and the rules it seeks enforced
R51: 'Hold at this stage, with a reason' and 'Decline to escalate' are two acts: holding names the stage proposed and keeps the escalation open; declining names the determination
R51: pausing sends the reason; a paused escalation proposes nothing and is resumed, the reason optional; each only in its own state
R51: the government's response is read at the response evaluation stage, from the replies received on the attached actions, with a reading and a reason
R51: stages are named in words, never shown by number: the ladder and the forms of each stage draw the stage's own word
R45, R50, R51: the matter's acts are the registry's; each form's act is drawn only for a member who may do it
R45, R50, R51 (writinghelp): the helper is drawn beside each field the design marks for it only while the assistant is reachable, and sends the words typed
R45 (writinghelp control): a help button that names no act sends no help request
R45, R50, R51 (R19): each form draws its sentences by their keys, and every act of the screen is explained by its own word
R45 (DEC-387): the matter with no determination yet says so and draws the escalation's acts as 'Not available yet'; recording reads 'Record this determination' and the form's own labels
R45 (DEC-387): revising reads 'Revise the determination' and 'What it replaces'; the rule's choice is 'Rule'

R50 (DEC-387): consequences read the matter's kinds and units, 'Describe them', 'Not known yet' and the reason behind a fold 'If you assess it yourself'; addressing reads 'The part', 'This part was' and 'Can't be undone'; a success reads 'When it changed'

R51 (DEC-387): attaching at the political accountability stage reads 'Its purpose' and its five options by key; the response reads the three readings by key and 'No response' for the reply; pausing reads 'Pause it'
R6 (DEC-387): the stages are named without a number: 'Move on to the next stage' carries the stage's name, and a stage listed on an action is 'at' its name

R56, R53 (re-walk 10): a phase that addresses someone outside with no branch for a hostile response is drawn in the design's own sentence, with the phase by name, never the plane's
R56 (re-walk 10 N7): a refusal of what an action rests on or advances, with the owner's reasons, draws those reasons whole and not the code's sentence that tells her to leave it out
R56 (re-walk 10 N7): the same when starting an option's action is refused; control: a refusal with no reasons draws the code's sentence alone

R56 (walk E C2a (1, 2)): a noncompliant determination against a standard whose binding is undetermined is drawn in the owner's words with the owner's why, never as 'does not bind'; the body is chosen among the team's offices and bodies and sent as the entity id
R56 (walk E C2b): the project's determinations are drawn each with its standards' outcomes, and recording one goes to its page
R56 (walk C C-M11): a concluded question no published case holds is drawn as concluded and never tickable; a published finding is offered as before

R56 (walk E K-words): a date check that cannot be told for want of a day names its option and phase by name, in the design's words, never ids; a regulated date before its phase draws names and days as dates
R56, R59 (walk E K4; walk C C-M17; DEC-439 K4): an option to an office, the press or an organization with its role or its body empty draws the owner's refusal naming the empty part
R56 (walk E K-new): a request for comment with no advancing leg is sent and the plane's own refusal, with its findings, is drawn; the leg defaults to 'Advances'
R56 (walk E K10): the door to the risk beside the tier refusal is its own control after the sentence, not run on from it; control: no refusal draws none
R56 (walk E H2): after a filing is recorded sent, its proposed next state is said in the owner's words with the way to the action's move; before, none
R56 (walk E H1): a request offers the team's named offices again, picked by label and asked about, and an empty press is refused in words, never silent
R56 (walk E K12): 'Waiting on' is drawn only while the action is neither resolved nor abandoned, whatever the plane says is owed
R58: a project with no dated event draws, in place of the event picker, the sentence that says so and where to record one; control: a project with an event draws the picker and not the sentence
R58: with no finding held to rest a determination on, the determination says so above Record a determination; control: with a published finding it does not
R58 (walk C C-M11): a concluded question no published case holds says it is concluded and not yet a finding, beside its title; control: with none such, the sentence is absent
R58: the determination's body is a choice among the team's offices and bodies, helped by its sentence; control: with the body read failed, neither the choice nor the help is drawn
R36: what is available by tier draws one row per kind of the answer {kinds, determinations, says}, never one blank row
R45 (b): a matter with no determination yet draws each act that needs one as unavailable, saying why, and offers to record a determination

R45 (c): recording a determination sends exactly what `determine` declares: the act, the findings it rests on, the rule, what it requires and what was done, the outcome, the question when unclear, the cause
R45 (C6): the event, the passage and the finding are chosen among what the project holds, and a determination missing one is refused in the words that name it
R45 (d): revising a determination names the one it replaces, opens with its values, and says why in the reason; the earlier is not edited
R45: the determination's refusals are drawn by their words (refusal.<CODE>); control: a recorded one draws none
R45: a member who may not act reads the read-only sentence and is offered no form and no act
R45: a determination already replaced is read and offers no form to record, revise or add to
R50: what the breach did is recorded with the rule it breached, who was affected, what it is measured in, the period and how it is known; each act sends its declared fields
R50: a recorded part is revised with the reason, only what was changed sent; control: the reason is the member's own
R50: whether a part was addressed is recorded with its evidence, its reason and, for an addressed one, in what way; control: a part not addressed names no way
R50: a success is recognised with what changed, when, the evidence, the order of events and, if said, the cause; control: the optional ones left out are not sent
R50: ending an escalation is refused in words while compliance is not restored or the consequences are undetermined or not addressed; control: an ended one draws no refusal
R51: an action is attached to the stage with the member's reason, picked from the determination's actions; at the political accountability stage with its purpose and the rules it seeks enforced
R51: 'Hold at this stage, with a reason' and 'Decline to escalate' are two acts: holding names the stage proposed and keeps the escalation open; declining names the determination
R51: pausing sends the reason; a paused escalation proposes nothing and is resumed, the reason optional; each only in its own state
R51: the government's response is read at the response evaluation stage, from the replies received on the attached actions, with a reading and a reason
R51: stages are named in words, never shown by number: the ladder and the forms of each stage draw the stage's own word
R45, R50, R51: the matter's acts are the registry's; each form's act is drawn only for a member who may do it
R45, R50, R51 (writinghelp): the helper is drawn beside each field the design marks for it only while the assistant is reachable, and sends the words typed
R45 (writinghelp control): a help button that names no act sends no help request
R45, R50, R51 (R19): each form draws its sentences by their keys, and every act of the screen is explained by its own word
R45 (DEC-387): the matter with no determination yet says so and draws the escalation's acts as 'Not available yet'; recording reads 'Record this determination' and the form's own labels
R45 (DEC-387): revising reads 'Revise the determination' and 'What it replaces'; the rule's choice is 'Rule'

R50 (DEC-387): consequences read the matter's kinds and units, 'Describe them', 'Not known yet' and the reason behind a fold 'If you assess it yourself'; addressing reads 'The part', 'This part was' and 'Can't be undone'; a success reads 'When it changed'

R51 (DEC-387): attaching at the political accountability stage reads 'Its purpose' and its five options by key; the response reads the three readings by key and 'No response' for the reply; pausing reads 'Pause it'
R6 (DEC-387): the stages are named without a number: 'Move on to the next stage' carries the stage's name, and a stage listed on an action is 'at' its name

R21, R32 (C94): the hold screen names who marked what wants a hold by handle, and the stake names who set it
R25: a project with one open plan opens that plan at once, with no list; the read is `plans` for the project
R25: several live plans, or only closed ones, are listed: live first (open, paused), newest first, then closed; each row a reference with its state and who opened it
R25: a project with no plan says where one is started, with no list and no empty heading; a failed read is drawn failed, never as no plan
R25: control: a plan id as the subject opens that plan as before; the back step lists the project's plans instead of opening it again
R44 (a): 'Add an option' sends the declared names only: with nothing more given it sends the line, kind and matter alone (no addressee, dates, tier, lobbying or enforces)
R44 (a): the addressee is sent as the plane's shape for each of the five choices, never a private individual; 'no one in particular' sends none
R44 (a): the dates that bind an option each carry their basis; 'add another' (up to 20) adds a line; an empty line sends nothing
R44 (a): the tier is sent only when one is chosen ('not assessed yet' sends none); lobbying sends the mark and the requirement it seeks
R44 (a): each refusal of 'Add an option' is drawn by its two sentences, beside the act; control: an option the plane takes draws none
R44 (b): a scenario lays out more than one phase, each with its name, options, start, check-back days, test and where each judgement goes
R44 (b): each refusal of a scenario is drawn by its two sentences, beside the act; control: a scenario the plane takes draws none
R44 (c): an option can be marked done or blocked, or returned to undecided, each sending its reason; never the mark it already has
R44 (c): a reminder (which date of the option, on what day) goes with the choice; none asked sends none; control: no dates, no reminder control
R44 (c): each refusal of a decision is drawn by its words beside the act: no reason, a reminder that is not for a choice or names no date of the option, no such option, a closed plan
R53: an option with no summary is named by its place in the list, a phase with no name by its place in its scenario, never by an id, wherever it is drawn
R53: the Judge control is drawn only once the checkpoint is due, by the page's clock; before, the day it can be judged; control: due today or earlier draws Judge
R53: a judgement is drawn as the words 'met' and 'not met', never the raw value: the judged phase, the control's choices and the check that a judgement leads nowhere
R44 (registry): the assistant's help with words is drawn on the option's line and detail and the close note only while the assistant is reachable; control: unreachable draws none

R44 (DEC-387): 'Add an option' reads the design's rows: the kinds, who it is directed to, the role and the date, the tier, seeking enforcement and its 'None'; control: the case list is not the table's

R44 (DEC-387): deciding the options reads the design's rows: marking done and blocked and returning to undecided on a row; 'Choose them', 'Decline them' and 'Mark them blocked' on the picked ones; the reminder's 'Which date'
R44 (DEC-387): a scenario's phase reads the design's rows: 'A phase', its options, when it starts, which phase and 'No phase' for where each judgement goes

R1, R44 (c) (C53): a chosen option with dates draws the Set-reminder act and the day it holds, read from the record; the act sends the choice with the reminder; control: an option with none draws the act only
